payload.headline: AMD drops 7.72% to 489.19 on reported short-seller China claims; still above value

summary.thesis: AMD's business is getting stronger fast, but even after today's drop the price sits well above every fair-value estimate in our data.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a much lower price. Swing: wait until the news settles and the price shows where it holds.
summary.act_at: Long-term buy case starts at 333.38; no swing trade above 451.0 until it holds

payload.happening: AMD fell 7.72% to 489.19 after CNBC reported a short-seller report alleging hidden exposure to China. The claims come from the short seller, and no company filing confirms them. The next earnings report is on 2027-02-02, so the price will move on the news before any new numbers arrive.
payload.business: The latest filing (2026-11-04) shows a business that is speeding up. Sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier, up from 37.85% two quarters ago. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 17.72% from 8.78%. Free cash flow, the cash left after investment, reached 7.1B over twelve months, up from 5.4B. AMD has more cash than debt (net cash 8.7B), so its finances are safe. Analysts have raised next-year earnings estimates by 11.3% in 30 days. Today's news hits sentiment right away. It touches the business only if the claims are true and China demand or export rules hurt sales. Our data has no breakdown of sales by region or segment, so the size of that exposure cannot be checked here. The filing points to two real business risks. Inventory is up 57% while sales are up 45%, and unsold stock can force price cuts. The 18% operating margin is also near the top of its 5-year range, and peaks like that tend to fade (general knowledge).

worth.text: Each valuation method puts fair value far below 489.19. A discounted cash flow model estimates what future cash is worth today. It gives 143.73 to 217.08, with a base case of 183.92. AMD's own price-to-sales history (price divided by yearly sales) gives 179.24 to 333.38. The gap comes from the growth assumption. The model caps starting cash-flow growth at 30%, which is worth about 184.49 a share. The market price implies starting growth of about 58.3%, while analysts expect next-year EPS growth of 118%. The other multiples say the same thing. The price is 106.6 times trailing earnings but 27.7 times next year's estimate. So the price only works if those high estimates come true. Price-to-sales is 17.7, against a peer median of 12.8, and sits in the 92nd percentile of AMD's own 5 years. Margins matter too. If operating margin fell to 13%, the model value drops to 97.39.
worth.key_assumption: Starting cash-flow growth: the model caps it at 30% (about 184.49 a share), while the price implies about 58.3%, so the price depends on analysts' 118% next-year EPS growth coming true.

bull: Growth is accelerating: quarterly sales rose 44.68% year over year, up from 37.85% two quarters earlier.
Profitability doubled: operating margin rose to 17.72% from 8.78%, and free cash flow grew to 7.1B from 5.4B.
Estimates are rising: next-year EPS of 17.64 is up 11.3% in 30 days, which puts the price at 27.7 times next year's earnings.
bear: The price of 489.19 is above the top of every fair-value method, the highest being 333.38.
It is expensive next to peers: price-to-sales of 17.7 against a peer median of 12.8, in the 92nd percentile of its own 5-year range.
Inventory up 57% against sales up 45% could squeeze margins, and an operating margin of 13% would cut model value to 97.39.

levels.what: Today's close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a buy price.
Bottom of the 451.0–469.22 support zone. A close below it would mean the selloff is deepening, but the price would still be above fair value.
Top of the fair-value range. The valuation case for buying starts here.

longterm.why: The business keeps improving, but the price needs growth far beyond the model's 30% cap. Today's drop still leaves it well above the highest fair value of 333.38.

swing.why: The price fell into the 480.33–502.6 zone and sits below its 20-day average (513.7) and 50-day average (554.93). With an average daily range (ATR) of 43.48, one normal day could reach the 451.0–469.22 support or the 517.35 resistance. The short-seller news is unresolved, so a setup needs either a hold above 451.0 or a close back above 517.35.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-02-02 are far off, but options priced moves of 6.2% by 2026-11-20 and 16.4% by 2026-12-18, so any company reply to the short-seller report could move the price before then.

change_mind: The price reaches 333.38 or lower with no filing confirming the reported China exposure. That would open the long-term buy case.
A filing confirms material China exposure, or the 2027-02-02 report shows EPS below the 2.72 low estimate. Either would weaken the growth case behind the 17.64 next-year EPS estimate.
A close below 424.03, the bottom of the lower support zone, would break the trading range and rule out a swing entry.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still wait, because the 7.72% drop to 489.19 on a reported short-seller allegation leaves the price far above the 333.38 top of fair value.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
